<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 /><noinclude>{{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} </noinclude><section begin=par /><!-- no section needed -->is found under the preformative in {{GHGheb|text=הֱקִלֹּתַ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=44}}, and a {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} occurs before {{GHGheb|text=ח}} (with a virtual sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ח}}) in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=הַֽחִתֹּ֫תָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=6|verse=13}}—in all these cases before {{GHGheb|text=חִ}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִלּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=3}}, see above, p: on {{GHGheb|text=וְהַחְתַּתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=37}}, see below, dd.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|x}}
7. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} of verbs whose second radical is a guttural, ''ă'' is retained ({{GHGpar|22|d}}) in the second syllable instead of ''ĕ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=25}}: so also with {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, as {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫צַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=9}}—but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫פֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|y}}
8. Aramaïzing forms (but cf. Rem. {{GHGpar|67|g}}) in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} are, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּסֵּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=18}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju.|chapter=18|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּמֵּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=21}}, but read {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תֶּ֫מֶר}} from {{GHGheb|text=מָרָה}}: {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכְּתוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=44}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=45}}), but {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּסֵּ֫בּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַחֵל|translate=profanabo}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=תַּתֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=3}}; without elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|53|q}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהַתֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=27}}, but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהָתֵ֫לוּ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּהָתֵ֫לּוּ}}; with ''î'' in the second syllable {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=45|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַנַּשִּׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=30}}; in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הִזִּי֫לוּהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=8}}. In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֻמְּכוּ|translate=they are brought low}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּת|translate=he is smitten}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=12}} (''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּ֫תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=7}}); in {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻחָֽקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּ֑תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=20}} (so Baer, Ginsb., but ed. Mant., Jabl. {{GHGheb|text=יֻכָּתּוּ}}); with ''ŏ'' in the initial syllable, {{GHGheb|text=הָשַּׁמָּהֿ}} ({{GHGterm|infinitive}} with ''suffix'' = {{GHGheb|text=הָשַּׁמָּהּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|91|e}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=34}} f., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=36|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּהְשַׁמָּה}}, with irregular syncope for {{GHGheb|text=בְּהָשַּׁ׳}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=43}}.

{{center|IV. ''In General.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|z}}
9. Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} are most closely related as regards inflexion to verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (§ 72). The form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} is generally the shorter (cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}); in a few cases, however, the two classes exactly coincide, e.g. in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} and in the less common conjugations (see above, l).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|aa}}
10. The developed forms (with three radicals), as mentioned in ''a'', are especially frequent in the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}}, and the 3rd ''plur. perf. Qal'' (i.e. in forms without an afformative or with an afformative beginning with a vowel) of transitive verbs, or verbs, at any rate, expressing action, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סָבַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָֽבְבוּ}} (but before a suffix also {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וּנִי}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=סְבָב֫וּנִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁדּ֫וּנִי}} &c.); {{GHGheb|text=זָמַם}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָֽמֲמָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָֽפֲפוּ}}, &c. Sometimes the contracted, ''as well as'' the uncontracted form, is found, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּזַז|translate=to plunder, plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽזְזוּ}}; in other parts, only {{GHGheb|text=בָּזַ֫זְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=35}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=בַּזּ֫וֹנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=זָמַ֫מְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=14.15}} and {{GHGheb|text=זַמֹּ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=28}}. Other examples of biliteral forms in 2nd ''sing. masc.'' are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=32}}; in 1st ''sing.'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=9}}. A part from Qal the only example of a developed form is {{GHGheb|text=וְהַחְתַּתִּ֫יּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=37}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|bb}}
On the other hand, the biliteral forms are the more common in the 3rd ''sing.'' and ''plur.'' of perfects which are ''intransitive'', and express a state; cf. {{GHGheb|text=דַּק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=21}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=דָּ֑ק}}; elsewhere always a transitive verb); {{GHGheb|text=חַת}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫תָּה}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַר}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫רָה}} (for ''marrā''); {{GHGheb|text=צַר}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=צָ֫רָה}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=וְחָ֫רָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=11}}); {{GHGheb|text=רַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁח}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫חָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּם}} &c.; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫תּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מּוּ}} &c. (but on the tone, cf. ee below). Exception, {{GHGheb|text=עָֽשְׁשָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|cc}}
The intransitive but developed perfects {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽלֲלוּ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לּוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=חָלַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָֽדְדָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָֽדְדוּ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נָדָ֫דוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=סָרַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָֽשֲׁשָׁה}} (''plur.'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָשֵֽׁשׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=11}}), {{GHGheb|text=צָֽלֲלוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁחֲחוּ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫חוּ}}), almost all have, as Mayer Lambert observes, at least an active, not a stative meaning. Triliteral forms of the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} after {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} are {{GHGheb|text=לִסְבֹּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁדוֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=47|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִגְזׄז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=19}} (also {{GHGheb|text=לָגֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=13}}); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=לַחְמָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=14}}, in ''subordinate pause'', for {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲמַם}}; with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲנַנְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=18}}, and, from the same<section end=par67 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
